Blaise Pascal on humanity

Blaise Pascal (1623–1662) approaches humanity within Christian philosophy. Human greatness and misery reveal a divided condition; practical reason may wager where demonstrative certainty is unavailable. Systematically, the teaching links faith, reason, probability into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets humanity most directly—useful for searches such as “blaise pascal quotes on humanity.”
